title: Pinned real Ribasim allocation/supply observability bridge
purpose: Execute the pinned real Ribasim solver on existing upstream test fixtures and independently verify the demand/allocated/supplied observability contract before introducing a custom SWAP-Ribasim conflict model.

upstream_execution.toolchain: Use pinned Ribasim repository pixi environment and official generated-testmodel route.
upstream_execution.julia_project: Ribasim repository root Project.toml with local core source

fair_distribution.preregistered_expectation: For 25 same-priority UserDemand nodes whose total demand is twice available initial Basin storage over the one-day horizon, every allocated/demand ratio is 0.5 within upstream numerical tolerance.

level_demand.preregistered_expectation: For UserDemand node 3 priority 2, allocation result supplied values shifted by the documented one allocation record equal the interval-average integrated physical flow on link 2 within atol 1e-3.

two_basin_user_demand.preregistered_expectation: Physical flow from fallback Basin 4 to UserDemand 5 ramps linearly from 1e-3 to 2e-3 as preferred Basin 3 supply decays, within atol 5e-6.

hypotheses: The pinned Ribasim source executes successfully for all three selected upstream fixtures.

Real Ribasim exposes demand, allocated and supplied as distinct allocation-result concepts; supplied is independently reproducible from physical linkflow with its documented one-allocation-period lag.
In the fair-distribution scarcity fixture, real allocated/demand equals 0.5 for every UserDemand, demonstrating executable allocation under scarcity rather than merely source-code structure.
In the two-source UserDemand fixture, route priority changes which source link supplies water while physical total demand remains supported; the fallback link follows the upstream preregistered ramp.
No comparison in DUMMY-19A treats allocated flow as physical supplied water.
No DUMMY-19A result may be interpreted as equivalence between Ribasim smooth physical reduction and the dummy hard active-set hmin.
A successful bridge binds stage1 observability only; it does not yet reproduce the DUMMY-15 two-recipient demand-priority conflict.
forbidden: no modification of pinned Ribasim source
no claim of full Ribasim network-optimizer equivalence
no claim that supplied output is same-row aligned with allocation
no tuning after observing real-Ribasim output
